evidence.claim: Walmart U.S. had fiscal 2025 net sales of $462.4 billion and markets merchandise under private brands including Allswell, Athletic Works, bettergoods, Equate, and others.
Seneca Foods discloses private-label products for retailers and sales through supermarkets, mass merchandisers, limited-assortment stores, club stores, and dollar stores.
Seneca conducts its business almost entirely in food packaging, which comprised approximately 98% of fiscal 2025 net sales.

Neogen develops, manufactures, and markets food-safety products including diagnostic test kits and complementary products sold to food producers and processors to detect pathogens, allergens, toxins, residues, sanitation issues, and other risks.
Neogen states that no single customer or distributor accounted for 10% or more of revenues in fiscal 2025, 2024, or 2023.

SPS Commerce describes itself as a global supply-chain network connecting retailers, brands, distributors, manufacturers, and logistics providers; its 2025 10-K references onboarding programs and supplier scorecarding.
SPS Commerce reported more than 50,000 recurring-revenue customers across retail, grocery, distribution, supply, manufacturing, and logistics in its February 2026 company release.
evidence.source_title: SPS Commerce Introduces MAX, New Capabilities Embedded in SPS’ Agentic Supply Chain Network

memory_update.text: SENEA is a priority underfollowed candidate for the private-label/value-retail food-input lane because it directly discloses private-label retail products and channel exposure to mass, club, dollar, limited-assortment, and grocery outlets.

NEOG is a second-order compliance/testing candidate: not a private-label manufacturer, but potentially exposed to retailer qualification requirements through food-safety diagnostics, sanitation, allergen, pathogen, and traceability workflows.
SPSC is a retailer-supplier execution network candidate, potentially tied to EDI, supplier onboarding, fulfillment, scorecarding, and retail trading-partner compliance complexity.

Packaging/label converter lane still needs a focused pass; possible next names to test include SON, GPK, AVY, SEE, and smaller packaging distributors/converters, but current pass prioritized private-label food and compliance infrastructure.
TreeHouse Foods would have been a high-relevance private-label food candidate, but it is no longer US-listed after the February 11, 2026 Investindustrial acquisition.

node: Private-label and value-retail inputs: food, household goods, packaging, labels, and compliance
summary: Expanded the node through an underfollowed discovery lens. The strongest public-market map is not the obvious retailer itself, but small/mid-cap suppliers and compliance/execution infrastructure that help retailers run private-label and value-channel programs: packaged-food private-label suppliers, food-safety testing systems, and retail trading-partner networks. TreeHouse Foods would have been a core private-label food candidate, but it was acquired and delisted on February 11, 2026, so it is treated as a private-company context marker rather than an investable US-listed candidate.
